# dsh-user-preferences

Replacement for `dsh-user-prompt`. Injects your standing preferences into every model request.
The h
ost half avoids coupling to the settings service and handles optional-service and file errors withou
t failing prompt assembly. A malformed package or missing hard dependency can still prevent activati
ailing prompt assembly. A malformed package or missing hard dependency can still prevent activation.
## Files (edit in any editor; changes apply on the next request, no restart)
| File | Scope |

| `<dshHome>/preferences/global.md` | all sessions (`dshHome` = `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh`) |
| `<proje
ct>/.dsh/preferences.md` | nearest to the session cwd; walks up, stops at the repo root (`.git`) or

`~` |
| `<dshHome>/preferences/settings.json` | `{ "enabled": true, "mode": "section" \| "context" }
`, overrides plugin config live |
Project text takes priority over global text when the budget (`maxChars`, default 20000) is exceeded

.
`` are stripped, so you can leave notes to yourself.
## Modes

- `section` (default): merged into the system prompt (highest authority); `{{...}}` stays literal.
-
`context`: separate user-role snapshot; every `{{` is defused so the renderer cannot throw.
## Startup resilience
- Only `systemPrompt` is a hard dependency; commands / connection are attached lazily via `ctx.injec

t`.
- It does not use the `settings` service; invalid settings-file values fall back at runtime.
- P
rompt registrations and optional attachments are guarded, so an individual registration failure is l

ogged instead of escaping `apply()`.
- Providers never throw: bad JSON, unreadable or oversized file

s, a directory in place of a file,
a hostile agent shape all degrade to "inject nothing" plus one de

duplicated log line.
- Transient read errors fall back to the last good content.
## Commands
`/preferences` shows the status. `/preferences path` prints the global file path.
## Install (desktop profile, local development)
1. Back up the profile's `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `cordis.patch.y

ml` and copy the old prompt to `<dshHome>/preferences/global.md`.
2. From the desktop profile direct
ory, use the profile's pnpm runtime to add `link:D:/Programs/dsh-user-preferences`; include `dsh-use
r-preferences` in `dsh.profile.bundles` and remove `dsh-user-prompt` from both dependencies and bund

les. Remove its `user-prompt` row from `cordis.patch.yml` without changing unrelated rows.
3. Reload
the profile (or restart DSH if its HMR watcher is unavailable). Verify that the effective bundle co
mposition contains `user-preferences` and not `user-prompt`, then confirm the Plugins → User prefere
nces card loads and saves, and prompt assembly contains the migrated text. The generated `cordis.yml
` can remain unchanged after a live HMR reconciliation; its timestamp alone does not prove whether t
he running Host reloaded.
The `link:` spec uses the local source directory. Keep that directory intact while installed. Revert
the backed-up profile files and reinstall its dependencies to roll back; do not overwrite the migra
ted global preferences file.
## Development

node --test test/core.test.mjs test/client.test.mjs test/rpc.test.mjs
node test/host-integration.mjs
# requires extracted host packages in .tmp/host
